title: MegIS: High-Performance, Energy-Efficient, and Low-Cost Metagenomic Analysis with In-Storage Processing
problem: Metagenomic analysis requires searching large databases to identify species and abundances in samples, but this causes significant data movement overhead from storage to the rest of the system. Existing metagenomic approaches cannot be directly implemented in-storage due to hardware limitations of modern SSDs.
motivation: Reducing data movement is critical for improving performance and energy efficiency in large-scale metagenomic analysis workloads.
method: MegIS uses hardware/software co-design with specialized task partitioning between in-storage and external processing, coordinates data and computation flow across storage boundaries, applies storage technology-aware algorithmic optimizations, implements intelligent data mapping, and deploys lightweight in-storage accelerators to efficiently execute metagenomic workloads within SSD constraints.
key_novelty: First in-storage processing system specifically designed for metagenomic analysis pipelines through careful co-design addressing SSD hardware limitations.
contributions: End-to-end in-storage processing system for metagenomic analysis
Task partitioning and data/computation flow coordination between in-storage and external processors
Storage technology-aware algorithmic optimizations and lightweight in-storage accelerators
2.7–37.2× speedup over software baselines with higher accuracy than PIM approaches

metrics.speedup: 2.7×–37.2× over software tools, 6.9×–100.2× over accuracy-optimized software, 1.5×–5.1× over PIM
metrics.accuracy: matches accuracy-optimized software tool, higher than PIM-based hardware accelerator
